merger_description:
HupCo Holdings Pty Ltd (**HupCo**) is a special purpose vehicle that has recently been incorporated and does not currently operate any business or hold any other interests (other than 100% of the interests in three special purpose vehicles established for the proposed acquisition).

Griffon Australia Holdings Pty Ltd (**Griffon Australia Holdings**), operating as AMES Australasia, is an Australian proprietary limited company and a subsidiary of Griffon Corporation, a U.S. diversified management and holding company that conducts business through wholly-owned subsidiaries. Griffon Corporation is listed on the New York Stock Exchange.

Griffon Australia Holdings operates the AMES business in Australia, which is a leading supplier of housing and gardening tools, storage solutions and outdoor lifestyle products. The AMES brand has a longstanding presence in the Australian market and supplies its products through major hardware and retail channels. Griffon AMES HoldCo LLC (**Griffon AMES**) is a U.S. limited liability company that currently holds all of the issued share capital of Griffon Australia Holdings.

HupCo (on behalf of the current AMES Australasia management team, and through its wholly-owned subsidiary HupCo ParentCo Pty Ltd) is seeking to acquire an indirect controlling interest in Griffon Australia Holdings. Griffon AMES will retain the remaining indirect interest in Griffon Australia Holdings, in each case through HupCo TopCo Pty Ltd. The transaction will be funded through a combination of equity contributed by HupCo, third-party debt financing and a retained interest held by Griffon AMES.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular, there is no horizontal overlap or vertical
relationships between the parties (or their connected entities) in the
supply of housing and gardening tools, storage solutions and
outdoor lifestyle products in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
